content:
Marissa Cole: quick q for release notes / customer comms on runtime 1.21: kernel auto-selection v2. what’s the *customer-visible* impact we should claim? and what risk language do we need so we’re not overpromising?

Paula Mendes: +1. specifically: is this “faster by default” vs “behind a gate”? also any wording for Dedicated/Private customers who ask if behavior changes.

Omar El-Sayed: customer-visible impact is mostly perf + stability, not API. No request/response schema changes. If enabled, expected improvements are lower p95/p99 and fewer throughput swings on mixed workloads across heterogeneous SKUs.
Omar El-Sayed: we should *not* claim universal speedups. It’s dependent on model family + seq length regime + GPU SKU. We’ve seen wins on A100/H100 in typical short-to-mid context, and we’re being cautious on long-context.

Yuki Sato: +1. v2 changes which kernel we pick (and adds better fallbacks). Users might notice different latency characteristics for the same model version if they’re opted into v2.
Yuki Sato: also important: determinism guarantee is “same inputs -> same selection decision” (model tag, seq bucket, SKU normalized, config). Not random/learned.

Marissa Cole: ok, so suggested framing is “improved kernel selection logic for better tail latency/throughput stability” and “no API changes”. but how do we say rollout status?

Connor O'Brien: release-wise: ships in 1.21, but default enablement is controlled by feature gate. Hosted: staged rollout by region/model allowlist. Dedicated/Private: opt-in or enabled per-customer after validation (esp constrained SKUs/driver versions).
Connor O'Brien: so language should explicitly say “available” not “enabled everywhere”.

Noah Patel: risk language: main risk is misclassification of long-context workloads leading to tail latency spikes on certain kernel/SKU combos. We have guardrails + denylist + rapid rollback, but call out “if you see regressions, disable v2 / pin kernel and contact support”.
Noah Patel: also mention: correctness is unchanged; selection only. But perf regressions are possible in edge cases (long prefill, unusual seq distributions, older drivers).

Paula Mendes: can we give a one-liner we can paste into the release notes + a short “known limitations” section?

Yuki Sato: draft release note snippet (feel free to edit):
“Kernel auto-selection v2: improved GPU kernel selection keyed on model family, sequence-length regime, and GPU SKU to reduce tail latency and improve throughput stability. No API changes. Rollout is gated and will be enabled gradually by model/region; Dedicated/Private customers can opt in with support.”

Omar El-Sayed: for known limitations / risk language, something like:
“- Performance may vary by model, prompt length, and GPU/driver. Long-context workloads are monitored closely; if you observe regressions, you can disable v2 or force a kernel via config/CLI and revert immediately.”

Marissa Cole: do we need to mention telemetry changes? customers sometimes ask.

Omar El-Sayed: we can mention “additional selection telemetry” but keep it non-scary: “adds observability to help debug performance issues.” No customer action required. Sampling controls in place.

Elliot Price: +1, but keep it tight. Suggested doc wording:
“Adds kernel selection decision telemetry (sampled) to support debugging and rollout monitoring.”
Elliot Price: also recommend we add a link in notes to the runbook / docs section “Overrides & Rollback” (especially for Dedicated/Private operators).

Paula Mendes: do we have a customer-friendly phrase for “feature gate + allowlist/denylist” that doesn’t sound like we’re uncertain?

Noah Patel: “staged rollout with automated safeguards” usually lands well. Optional line: “Includes safe fallbacks and rapid rollback controls.”

Connor O'Brien: +1. avoid saying “experimental”. this is “GA, staged enablement.”

Marissa Cole: ok final proposal:
1) Feature summary: improved kernel selection for lower tail latency + throughput stability, no API changes.
2) Rollout: staged enablement by region/model, Dedicated/Private opt-in initially.
3) Risks: perf may vary, long-context edge cases; mitigations: safeguards, overrides, rollback.
Marissa Cole: I’ll incorporate into release notes + comms doc. pls sanity check once I paste.

Yuki Sato: sounds good. :thumbsup:

Omar El-Sayed: :thumbsup: and I can provide the exact “disable v2 / force kernel” names once you have a draft (so we don’t publish wrong flags).

Elliot Price: same—tag me when ready and I’ll align wording with the docs section headers.

Paula Mendes: thanks all. I’ll update the customer-facing FAQ with the “staged rollout w/ safeguards” phrasing.

Marissa Cole: awesome, ty.
